title: Fibonacci EA v5.0 Asymmetric Profit Scale-Out Test (InpTP1ClosePct = 75.0%)
research_question: Does increasing InpTP1ClosePct from 50.0% to 75.0% increase realized net profitability and profit factor above baseline EXP-0008 ($577.65) while preserving the ~80% win rate and keeping max equity drawdown <= 8.0% on GBPUSD M15?
hypothesis: Closing 75% of position volume at the 10-pip mark (which has an empirical 80% hit rate) will bank greater immediate cash before market retracements to breakeven occur, lifting average win size, increasing total net profit above the baseline $577.65, and keeping max equity drawdown <= 8.0%.

facts: EXP-0008 demonstrated that holding positions with InpTP2Pips=30.0 is critical to prevent overtrading and preserve the 79.4% win rate.
EXP-0012 validation proved that the 10-pip TP1 hit rate is exceptionally high (80.27%), but runners often return to breakeven ($0) before reaching 30 pips, diluting the average win size to $15.14.
Closing 75% instead of 50% at TP1 increases the cash locked in at the 80%-win threshold by 50% without altering trade entries, trade frequency, or exit stop levels.
inferences: Front-loading the profit realization to the high-probability 10-pip level directly counters the 1:4.66 payoff asymmetry.
Leaving 25% of the position as a runner maintains the slot-blocking protection against overtrading while still capturing upside on extended market runs.
evidence: EXP-0008 total_trades=272, profit_factor=1.39, win_rate=79.38%, total_net_profit=577.65, equity_drawdown_maximal_percent=7.35

independent_variables.name: InpTP1ClosePct
independent_variables.rationale: Increase the scale-out portion at the high-probability 10-pip TP1 level to bank the majority of gains early.

assumptions: Broker trade volume step supports partial closure at 75% volume.
expected_observations: Total net profit will exceed the baseline $577.65.
falsification_conditions: Total net profit drops below baseline $577.65.
Maximum equity drawdown exceeds 8.0%, violating prop firm guard limits.
